metadata.name: neural-mcp
metadata.description: Neural network training and experimentation MCP server. Define, train, and evaluate PyTorch models with GPU acceleration. Supports hyperparameter tuning, experiment tracking, dataset management, and visualization of training dynamics.
metadata.pattern: Model Registry + Experiment Tracking + Long-Running Tasks

architecture.pattern_explanation: Model Registry: Central catalog of architectures (ResNet, MobileNet, custom). Experiment Tracking: Log metrics, hyperparameters, checkpoints per experiment. Long-Running Tasks: Training takes minutes to hours, use MCP Tasks with progress reporting.

model_id.purpose: Reference neural network model (architecture + optional weights)
model_id.lifetime: Session-scoped, can persist checkpoints to disk

experiment_id.purpose: Track training run with all metrics, hyperparameters, checkpoints

data_flow.typical_workflow_1: load_dataset(CIFAR10) → dataset_id → create_dataloader → dataloader_id → define_model(ResNet18) → model_id → train_model(model_id, dataloader_id) → experiment_id → plot_training_curves
data_flow.typical_workflow_2: define_model(custom) → model_id → tune_hyperparameters(model_id, dataset_id, param_grid) → tuning_id → best_params → train_model(model_id, hyperparams=best_params)
data_flow.cross_mcp_workflow: molecular-mcp generates trajectory data → neural-mcp.create_custom_dataset(data) → train_model (predict properties from MD data)

gpu_strategy.mixed_precision: torch.cuda.amp for faster training on modern GPUs

experiment_tracking.integration: Optional W&B integration for advanced users

enforced_questions.question: Should we support custom loss functions and optimizers?
enforced_questions.recommendation: Phase 1: Standard losses (CrossEntropy, MSE, BCE) and optimizers (SGD, Adam, AdamW). Phase 2: Custom via function strings.
enforced_questions.rationale: Standard covers 95% of use cases. Custom adds complexity (security: code injection risk).

enforced_questions.question: How to handle model checkpoints (large files, 100MB-10GB)?
enforced_questions.recommendation: Save to /tmp/neural-mcp-checkpoints/{experiment_id}/, return file paths not contents. Provide download/export tool.
enforced_questions.rationale: Checkpoints are binary and large. Return URIs, not inline data.

enforced_questions.question: Should we support distributed training (multi-GPU)?
enforced_questions.recommendation: Phase 1: Single GPU. Phase 2: DataParallel (simple multi-GPU). Phase 3: DistributedDataParallel (advanced).
enforced_questions.rationale: Single GPU covers most cases. Distributed adds significant complexity.

enforced_questions.question: What datasets to support out-of-box?
enforced_questions.recommendation: torchvision datasets (CIFAR10/100, MNIST, ImageNet subset), torchtext (basic), custom via arrays/files.
enforced_questions.rationale: torchvision is standard for vision. Custom datasets critical for real applications.

enforced_questions.question: How to visualize model internals (activations, gradients, weights)?
enforced_questions.recommendation: Phase 1: Training curves, confusion matrix, sample predictions. Phase 2: Grad-CAM, activation maps, weight histograms.
enforced_questions.rationale: Training curves are essential. Advanced visualizations are specialized.

tools.name: info
tools.description: Progressive discovery of Neural MCP capabilities. Explore model architectures, datasets, training options, and analysis tools.

tools.name: define_model
tools.description: Define neural network architecture. Supports built-in models (ResNet, MobileNet, etc.) from torchvision/timm, or custom architectures via layer specifications.

num_classes.description: Number of output classes (for classification). Required for built-in models.

pretrained.description: Load pretrained weights (ImageNet for vision models)

custom_layers.description: Layer specifications for custom architecture. Each: {type, params}

input_shape.description: Input shape [C, H, W] or [features]. Used for validation and custom models.

tools.relationships: Creates model for training or evaluation
use_cases: Load pretrained ResNet50 for transfer learning
Build custom CNN from layer specifications
user_stories: As a student, I want to train ResNet on CIFAR10
As a researcher, I want to define a custom architecture for my problem

required_functions: build_custom_model(layers) - construct nn.Sequential or custom nn.Module from layer specs
implementation_guide.usage_patterns: If architecture in registry, load from torchvision/timm. If custom, parse layer specs and build.
implementation_guide.pseudocode: if architecture == 'custom': model = build_custom_model(custom_layers, input_shape); elif architecture in TORCHVISION_MODELS: model = getattr(torchvision.models, architecture)(pretrained=pretrained); if num_classes != 1000: model.fc = nn.Linear(model.fc.in_features, num_classes); elif architecture in TIMM_MODELS: model = timm.create_model(architecture, pretrained=pretrained, num_classes=num_classes); num_params = sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters() if p.requires_grad); model_id = store_model(model); return {model_id: model_id, num_parameters: num_params, summary: str(model)[:500]}

tools.name: load_pretrained
tools.description: Load pretrained model from checkpoint file or model hub (Hugging Face, timm).

path_or_name.description: File path for checkpoint, model name for hub

architecture.description: Architecture name (required if loading checkpoint without metadata)

output_schema.pretrained_on: string - Dataset model was pretrained on (if known)

tools.relationships: Alternative to define_model for loading existing models

implementation_guide.pseudocode: if source == 'checkpoint': state_dict = torch.load(path_or_name); model = create_model(architecture); model.load_state_dict(state_dict); elif source == 'timm': model = timm.create_model(path_or_name, pretrained=True); elif source == 'huggingface': model = transformers.AutoModel.from_pretrained(path_or_name); model_id = store_model(model); return {model_id: model_id}

tools.name: load_dataset
tools.description: Load dataset from torchvision, torchtext, or Hugging Face datasets.

implementation_guide.usage_patterns: Map dataset name to torchvision class, build transform pipeline, instantiate dataset
implementation_guide.pseudocode: transform = build_transforms(transforms); dataset_class = getattr(torchvision.datasets, name); train = (split == 'train'); dataset = dataset_class(root=root, train=train, download=download, transform=transform); dataset_id = store_dataset(dataset); return {dataset_id: dataset_id, num_samples: len(dataset), num_classes: len(dataset.classes) if hasattr(dataset, 'classes') else None}

tools.name: create_dataloader
tools.description: Create DataLoader for batching and shuffling dataset during training.

num_workers.description: Number of data loading workers (0 for single-threaded)

implementation_guide.pseudocode: dataset = load_dataset(dataset_id); dataloader = DataLoader(dataset, batch_size=batch_size, shuffle=shuffle, num_workers=num_workers); dataloader_id = store_dataloader(dataloader); return {dataloader_id: dataloader_id, num_batches: len(dataloader)}

tools.name: train_model
tools.description: Train neural network on dataset. Returns task_id for async execution with progress tracking. Logs metrics per epoch to experiment.
tools.relationships: Core training tool. Produces experiment_id for analysis and checkpoints.
use_cases: Train ResNet18 on CIFAR10 for 50 epochs
Fine-tune pretrained model with early stopping
user_stories: As a student, I want to train a model and see training curves
As a researcher, I want to track experiments and compare hyperparameters

implementation_guide.usage_patterns: Create optimizer and loss, run training loop with progress reporting, log metrics per epoch, save checkpoints
implementation_guide.pseudocode: async def train(): model = load_model(model_id); train_loader = load_dataloader(train_dataloader_id); optimizer = create_optimizer(optimizer, model.parameters(), learning_rate); criterion = create_loss(loss_function); experiment_id = create_experiment(hyperparameters); device = 'cuda' if use_gpu and torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu'; model.to(device); async with tracked_task(task_id, ctx, epochs) as progress: for epoch in range(epochs): model.train(); total_loss = 0; for batch in train_loader: inputs, targets = batch; inputs, targets = inputs.to(device), targets.to(device); optimizer.zero_grad(); outputs = model(inputs); loss = criterion(outputs, targets); loss.backward(); optimizer.step(); total_loss += loss.item(); avg_loss = total_loss / len(train_loader); if val_dataloader_id: val_loss, val_acc = evaluate(model, val_loader, criterion, device); log_metrics(experiment_id, epoch, {train_loss: avg_loss, val_loss: val_loss, val_acc: val_acc}); else: log_metrics(experiment_id, epoch, {train_loss: avg_loss}); if epoch % checkpoint_every == 0: save_checkpoint(model, experiment_id, epoch); await progress.update(epoch, f'Epoch {epoch}/{epochs}, loss: {avg_loss:.4f}'); if lr_scheduler: scheduler.step(); if early_stopping and should_stop(early_stopping, metrics): break; save_final_checkpoint(model, experiment_id); return {experiment_id: experiment_id}; task_id = task_manager.create_task(train); return {task_id: task_id, experiment_id: generate_experiment_id()}
implementation_guide.metrics_logging: Store per-epoch metrics in SQLite: experiment_id, epoch, train_loss, val_loss, val_acc, lr
implementation_guide.checkpoint_format: Save as {experiment_id}_epoch_{epoch}.pth with model state_dict, optimizer state_dict, epoch, metrics

tools.performance: slow (minutes to hours depending on model size, dataset size, epochs)

tools.name: get_experiment_status
tools.description: Get training progress and current metrics for running or completed experiment.

implementation_guide.pseudocode: exp = experiment_db.get(experiment_id); task = task_manager.get_task(exp.task_id); return {status: task.state, current_epoch: exp.current_epoch, latest_metrics: exp.get_latest_metrics(), best_metrics: exp.get_best_metrics()}

tools.name: evaluate_model
tools.description: Evaluate trained model on test set. Computes loss and accuracy (or other metrics).

output_schema.inference_time_ms: number - Average inference time per sample

tools.relationships: Test model performance on held-out data
use_cases: Evaluate final model on test set

implementation_guide.pseudocode: model = load_model(model_id); test_loader = load_dataloader(test_dataloader_id); device = 'cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu'; model.to(device); model.eval(); all_preds, all_targets = [], []; with torch.no_grad(): for inputs, targets in test_loader: inputs = inputs.to(device); outputs = model(inputs); preds = outputs.argmax(dim=1); all_preds.extend(preds.cpu()); all_targets.extend(targets); from sklearn.metrics import accuracy_score, precision_recall_fscore_support; acc = accuracy_score(all_targets, all_preds); if 'precision' in metrics: prec, rec, f1, _ = precision_recall_fscore_support(all_targets, all_preds, average='macro'); return {metrics: {accuracy: acc, precision: prec, recall: rec, f1: f1}}

tools.performance: moderate (~seconds to minutes depending on test set size)

tools.name: plot_training_curves
tools.description: Generate training curves (loss, accuracy vs epoch) for experiment.
use_cases: Check for overfitting (train vs val loss divergence)

implementation_guide.pseudocode: exp = experiment_db.get(experiment_id); metrics_history = exp.get_metrics_history(); fig, axes = plt.subplots(len(metrics), 1); for i, metric in enumerate(metrics): axes[i].plot(metrics_history['epoch'], metrics_history[metric]); axes[i].set_ylabel(metric); plt.savefig(output_path); return {output_path: output_path}

tools.name: confusion_matrix
tools.description: Compute and visualize confusion matrix for classification model.

implementation_guide.pseudocode: model, test_loader = load_model_and_data(); all_preds, all_targets = get_predictions(model, test_loader); from sklearn.metrics import confusion_matrix; cm = confusion_matrix(all_targets, all_preds); import seaborn as sns; sns.heatmap(cm, annot=True, fmt='d', xticklabels=class_names, yticklabels=class_names); plt.savefig(output_path); acc_per_class = cm.diagonal() / cm.sum(axis=1); return {output_path: output_path, matrix: cm.tolist(), accuracy_per_class: acc_per_class.tolist()}

tools.name: tune_hyperparameters
tools.description: Automated hyperparameter search using grid search or random search. Returns best hyperparameters.

model_architecture.description: Model architecture to tune (will create fresh model for each trial)

param_grid.description: Hyperparameter search space. Keys are param names, values are arrays of options.

n_trials.description: Number of trials for random search

use_cases: Find best learning rate and optimizer

implementation_guide.pseudocode: async def tune(): if search_method == 'grid': import itertools; keys = param_grid.keys(); values = param_grid.values(); configs = [dict(zip(keys, v)) for v in itertools.product(*values)]; else: configs = random_sample_configs(param_grid, n_trials); results = []; async with tracked_task(task_id, ctx, len(configs)) as progress: for i, config in enumerate(configs): model_id = define_model(model_architecture); exp_id = train_model(model_id, train_dataloader_id, val_dataloader_id, epochs=epochs_per_trial, **config); await wait_for_experiment(exp_id); metrics = get_final_metrics(exp_id); results.append({config: config, metric_value: metrics[metric]}); await progress.update(i); best = max(results, key=lambda x: x['metric_value']) if mode == 'max' else min(results, key=...); store_tuning_results(tuning_id, results, best); return {best_params: best['config'], best_metric: best['metric_value'], all_results: results}; task_id = task_manager.create_task(tune); return {task_id: task_id, tuning_id: generate_tuning_id()}

tools.performance: very slow (hours for grid search with many combinations)

tools.name: get_model_summary
tools.description: Get detailed model architecture summary including layer-by-layer breakdown.

input_shape.description: Input shape for computing output shapes per layer

output_schema.layers: array<object> - Layer-by-layer breakdown {name, type, params, output_shape}
output_schema.model_size_mb: number - Approximate model size in memory

required_functions: torchsummary or torchinfo for detailed summary
implementation_guide.pseudocode: model = load_model(model_id); from torchinfo import summary; summary_obj = summary(model, input_size=(batch_size, *input_shape), verbose=0); return {total_parameters: summary_obj.total_params, trainable_parameters: summary_obj.trainable_params, layers: parse_layer_info(summary_obj)}

tools.name: export_model
tools.description: Export trained model to various formats for deployment (ONNX, TorchScript, SavedModel).

implementation_guide.pseudocode: model = load_model(model_id); dummy_input = torch.randn(1, *input_shape); if format == 'onnx': torch.onnx.export(model, dummy_input, output_path, input_names=['input'], output_names=['output']); elif format == 'torchscript': traced = torch.jit.trace(model, dummy_input); traced.save(output_path); file_size = os.path.getsize(output_path) / (1024**2); return {output_path: output_path, file_size_mb: file_size}

critical_patterns: Use MCP Tasks for training (always async)
Progress reporting every epoch (or batch for very long epochs)
Store checkpoints to disk, return paths not contents
Log metrics to SQLite experiment DB for querying
GPU memory management: clear cache between experiments if needed
security_requirements: Custom model architectures: validate layer types against whitelist
No arbitrary code execution (no eval, exec)
Checkpoint paths: validate no path traversal
Dataset downloads: validate URLs if custom datasets allowed
performance_optimization: Use mixed precision (torch.cuda.amp) for faster training on modern GPUs
DataLoader num_workers > 0 for parallel data loading
Pin memory for faster GPU transfer
Gradient accumulation for effective large batch sizes
testing_strategy: Unit tests: model creation, dataset loading (small datasets)
Integration tests: short training runs (5 epochs, tiny model)
Regression tests: compare metrics on known dataset (MNIST, 10 epochs should reach ~98%)
GPU tests: verify GPU utilization during training
handoff_checklist: ✓ Model registry with torchvision + timm models
✓ Custom model builder from layer specs
✓ Training loop with MCP Tasks and progress
